item: A full rebuild of the keyword rollup that stops after its swap-in is not followed by an incremental refresh that merges the tail again
summary: refresh_keyword_daily enters the full branch at an EQUAL epoch only when a table is missing (a store from before keyword_meta existed, or a dropped table). build_keyword_daily swaps the new keyword_daily in, fills keyword_meta and only then moves the watermark, each its own commit, so a stop after the swap-in left built_epoch valid over the OLD watermark and over tables that were all present again: the next refresh was incremental and merged the tail the swapped-in table already held, over a part-filled keyword_meta. Measured on the test world (in-memory DuckDB store over a 4-article corpus, 24 terms; keyword_meta dropped, the stop induced as an OperationalError on the second keywords SELECT with batch_size 2): the next refresh was incremental, 11 of 24 terms differed from a fresh full build and keyword_meta held 11 of 24 rows. The full branch now voids a standing built_epoch before it starts (the same VOIDED_BUILT_EPOCH as the incremental merge, R352) and puts it back after the build, so the next refresh is a full rebuild; nothing changes when built_epoch is absent or already voided, and a rebuild at a different epoch was already full. The stop is induced and the field cause inferred. Red before: the new test fails on the old code (mode incremental, not full).
